title: Assurance of Salvation
definition: Assurance of Salvation is the Spirit-supported confidence that believers truly belong to Christ and are kept by His grace.
summary: Assurance of Salvation is the Spirit-supported confidence that believers truly belong to Christ and are kept by His grace.
christFocus: Jesus gives His sheep eternal life, holds them securely, and sends the Holy Spirit to bear witness that they belong to God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Assurance does not mean believers never struggle with doubt. It means confidence can rest on the promises of God, the finished work of Christ, and the witness of the Holy Spirit rather than on changing emotions.

Scripture gives assurance through the Gospel, the fruit of faith, the Spirit’s witness, and God’s preserving grace. The believer looks to Christ first, then sees evidence of His work in a life being drawn toward repentance, faith, and obedience.

Assurance is not pride. It is humble confidence in the Savior who saves completely. Weak faith may still cling to a strong Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many believers carry fear that God will finally reject them because they still struggle. Assurance helps troubled hearts distinguish conviction from condemnation and weakness from abandonment.

This doctrine is deeply pastoral for people shaped by shame, addiction, or spiritual abuse. Christ does not invite His people into endless uncertainty; He calls them to trust His promise.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your doubts to Christ instead of hiding them. Return to the Gospel, examine your life honestly, ask the Holy Spirit for assurance, and let God’s promises teach you to follow Jesus with grateful confidence.
